Torn goes further than ambivalent: the two feelings stop coexisting and start ripping, so that choosing either way feels like a loss.

Mixed feelings contain both good and bad reactions, in any proportion — a mild, catch-all report that says nothing about strength. Ambivalent is more exact: two opposing feelings, each strong, held at the same time and pulling with real force.
